q1: SELECT b1.name AS bar1, b2.name AS bar2 FROM bar AS b1, bar AS b2 WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT s1.beer FROM serves AS s1 WHERE s1.bar = b1.name AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = b2.name AND s2.beer = s1.beer)) AND EXISTS(SELECT s2.beer FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = b2.name AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s1 WHERE s1.bar = b1.name AND s1.beer = s2.beer))
q2: SELECT DISTINCT v1.bar, v2.bar FROM serves AS v1, serves AS v2 WHERE v1.beer IN (v2.beer) AND v1.bar <> v2.bar
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT b1.name AS bar1, b2.name AS bar2 FROM bar AS b1, bar AS b2 WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT s1.beer FROM serves AS s1 WHERE s1.bar = b1.name AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = b2.name AND s2.beer = s1.beer)) AND EXISTS(SELECT s2.beer FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = b2.name AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s1 WHERE s1.bar = b1.name AND s1.beer = s2.beer))
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT v1.bar, v2.bar FROM serves AS v1, serves AS v2 WHERE v1.beer IN (v2.beer) AND v1.bar <> v2.bar
counterexample: INSERT INTO Bar (name, address) VALUES ('B1', 'Address1'), ('B2', 'Address2'); INSERT INTO Beer (name, brewer) VALUES ('B1 beer', 'Brewer1'), ('B2 beer', 'Brewer2'); INSERT INTO Serves (bar, beer, price) VALUES ('B1', 'B1 beer', 5.00), ('B2', 'B2 beer', 4.50);
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent. Q1 is checking for bars that serve a unique beer (no other bar serves that beer) and another bar that does not serve that beer. Q2 is checking for pairs of bars where one bar serves a beer that the other bar also serves.
counterexample_dsp: Two bars, 'B1' and 'B2', where 'B1' serves beer 'B1 beer' and 'B2' serves beer 'B2 beer', and 'B1 beer' is not served by 'B2' and 'B2 beer' is not served by 'B1'.
